title: How much cheaper must an urgency cue be for the urgent before a door robot can rely on it?
summary: society-fakeurgency gave everyone the same signalling cost and found no gain for urgent people. Here the urgent pay a share rho of what normal people pay. With 30% robots, 20% urgent people, collision cost 3 and dithering cost 1, rho = 0.5 gives urgent people +0.14 per encounter over yield-all at a normal cost of 0.6, rho = 0.25 gives +0.29 and rho = 0 gives +0.44 (perfect reading gives +0.45); at rho ≥ 0.75 there is no gain. A 10% misreading rate cuts the usable rho to 0.75 or below at the edge and 20% to 0.4. The crowd, robots included, is worse off than under yield-all in all 35 cells (+0.045 to +0.28), but that loss is robot-robot collisions inherited from society-fakeurgency (both robots go and collide, cost 3 against 1): with robots yielding to each other, perfect reading leaves the crowd 0.135 better off and 25 of 35 cells favour it. The no-gain threshold rho ≤ about 0.5 holds at a normal cost of 0.6, not at 0.4. Mean field from society-fakeurgency, which was checked by simulation. Assumed, not sourced: rho and the signal costs (swept), round-figure door costs, logit sharpness, no robot learning, random pairing.
lede: how much cheaper must an urgency cue be for the urgent before a door robot can rely on it? At a normal signal cost of 0.6, urgent people must pay at most about half; the crowd's loss under the cue is robot-robot collisions, not the cue.
